blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the very top, tax is not a function. It is a discipline of leadership that shapes how a company relates to the countries it lives in, the employees it rewards, the shareholders it serves and the society it quietly depends on. Done with honesty, stewardship and patience, it becomes one of the quieter forms of good corporate citizenship — and one of the longer-lasting.

The principles are simple. Pay what you owe, clearly and calmly. Document everything, so that any future question has an honest answer ready. Treat tax authorities as long-term partners, not as opponents. Bring tax into strategic conversations early, and speak in the language of the business rather than the language of the rulebook. Protect the reputation these habits build, because it is worth more than any saving a shortcut could deliver.

Over a decade, leaders who live by these principles find that tax stops being a source of anxiety and becomes a source of quiet confidence. Their companies rarely appear in the news for the wrong reasons; their regulators answer the phone. And when a difficult year arrives — as it always eventually does — the goodwill they have quietly built is already there, waiting to help them through. That, in the end, is the real product of treating tax as a leadership discipline.

items.q: According to the text, at the very top, tax is best understood as…
options: a cost centre to be minimised
items.why: "At the very top, tax is not a function. It is a discipline of leadership."

items.q: How does the text say tax authorities should be treated?
options: As a source of unavoidable friction
As auditors to be kept at arm's length
items.why: "Treat tax authorities as long-term partners, not as opponents."

items.q: The phrase "speak in the language of the business rather than the language of the rulebook" suggests that a tax leader should…
options: leave strategy to the finance team
frame tax in terms of commercial impact and strategy
quote regulations verbatim to the board
items.why: Inferência: falar a "língua do negócio" é traduzir o tema fiscal em termos de estratégia e impacto comercial, não recitar o manual.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A well-timed shortcut is justified if it delivers a large saving.
Goodwill built quietly pays off in difficult years.
Reputation is worth more than a one-off tax saving.
Good documentation protects a company years later.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que a reputação vale mais do que qualquer economia de um atalho — logo, discordaria de justificar o atalho.

items.q: The detail that such companies' "regulators answer the phone" most strongly implies that…
options: regulators are legally required to respond quickly
regulation in their sector is unusually light
years of honest conduct earn a company access and trust
items.why: Inferência: o acesso é fruto da boa vontade acumulada por condutas honestas ao longo dos anos, não de obrigação ou sorte.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James encerrando o programa de liderança fiscal com a diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So we come to the end of two years together, and I want to close not with a checklist but with a way of seeing.

When we started, most of you thought of tax as something that happened after the decisions were made — a bill to be minimised, a return to be filed. I hope you now see it differently. The teams that sleep well on Sunday evenings are not the ones with the cleverest structures. They are the ones who documented honestly, who picked up the phone to the authorities before there was a problem, and who protected a reputation that took a decade to build.

Here at Czarnikow, we sit in a dozen jurisdictions, and that multiplies every judgement you make. A shortcut that looks clever in one country can cost you trust in five others. So my ask is simple. Bring tax into the room early, while the strategy is still soft enough to shape. Speak in the language of the business, not the rulebook. And when the difficult year comes — and it always does — you will find the goodwill you built quietly is already there, waiting.

That, more than any saving, is what leadership in this discipline actually looks like.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does James choose to close the two-year programme?
options: With a review of each jurisdiction's rules
With a way of seeing rather than a checklist
With targets for next year's tax savings
items.why: "I want to close not with a checklist but with a way of seeing."

items.q: At the start of the programme, how did most of the executives think of tax?
options: As something that happened after the decisions were made
As the heart of every strategic choice
As a partnership with the authorities
items.why: "most of you thought of tax as something that happened after the decisions were made."

items.q: According to James, the teams who "sleep well on Sunday evenings" are those who…
options: documented honestly and engaged authorities early
items.why: "not the ones with the cleverest structures… who documented honestly, who picked up the phone to the authorities before there was a problem."

items.q: Why does James stress that Czarnikow "sits in a dozen jurisdictions"?
options: To explain why local tax rates differ
To recommend consolidating into fewer countries
Because operating across borders multiplies the weight of every judgement
Because most jurisdictions share the same rules
items.why: Inferência: a presença multi-jurisdicional amplia cada decisão — um atalho num país pode custar confiança em cinco outros.

items.q: What does James imply by asking the team to bring tax in "while the strategy is still soft enough to shape"?
options: Strategy should be kept deliberately vague
Tax teams should avoid strategic meetings
Tax input has more influence before decisions harden
Tax should be raised only once the strategy is final
items.why: Inferência: envolver o tema fiscal cedo, enquanto a estratégia ainda é maleável, permite influenciá-la — depois de pronta, resta apenas cumprir.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Managing tax with genuine stewardship means guarding it as something held in trust." Stewardship is…
options: strict adherence to a written manual
aggressive pursuit of the lowest bill
responsible care of something on behalf of others
delegation of a task to advisers
items.why: Stewardship = zelo/custódia: cuidar de algo confiado a você, em nome de terceiros.

items.q: "Paying fairly is a quiet form of corporate citizenship." This phrase refers to…
options: the legal nationality of a company
a company acting as a responsible member of society
items.why: Corporate citizenship = cidadania corporativa: a empresa se comportando como membro responsável da sociedade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He refused to treat the auditor as an ___; he saw her as a partner."
items.why: Opponent = oponente/adversário — o oposto do parceiro que a lição recomenda ser.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Any saving from a ___ was dwarfed by the reputational damage it caused."
items.why: Shortcut = atalho: o ganho aparente é apagado pelo dano à reputação.

items.q: "After a decade of honest filing, tax became a source of quiet confidence." Here confidence means…
items.why: Confidence = confiança: uma segurança serena, oposta à ansiedade que o tema costumava provocar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de liderança fiscal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the tax strategy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We agreed the documentation policy but never followed through on it." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto — não foi levado adiante.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the aggressive structure." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "A last-minute shortcut will not move the needle on the group's tax position." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, negado.

items.q: "Bring the tax team in early so nothing slips through the cracks." This means so that nothing…
items.why: Slip through the cracks = passar despercebido, ser esquecido por falta de atenção.
